chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from al-Nawfali, from al-Sakuni, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
The Messenger of Allah (peace be upon him and his family) said: 'There is no cutting (of the limb) for fruit, nor for sap, and the sap is the fat of the palm tree.'

key_terms.ثَمَر: Fruit (specifically of palm trees in this context)
key_terms.شَحْم: Fat (used metaphorically for rich essence or sap)
key_terms.قَطْع: Amputation (of the hand) as a criminal punishment

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on amputation for stealing palm fruit or sap in Shia jurisprudence?
ai.summary: This hadith from Al-Kafi clarifies that the hadd punishment of amputation does not apply to the theft of palm produce, specifically distinguishing between the fruit and the sap (kasar), which is described as the tree's 'fat' or rich essence. Scholarly commentary notes that this ruling reflects the principle of *qillat* (minimum threshold) not being met for these abundant, easily accessible goods, or alternatively, that they are considered distinct from the primary stored wealth (*mal*) typically subject to *qat'*. The description of sap as 'fat' highlights its nutritional and economic value, yet its transient nature exempts it from the strictest criminal penalties.
